passage.title: Inventions
paragraphs: Inventors need imagination and creativity. The Wright brothers tried to fly many times, but they failed. Finally, they succeeded in 1903. Now that we have planes, our world is very different.

Louis Braille had an accident when he was three. The accident left him blind. At that time, it was hard for blind children to read. They had to touch raised letters. It was easy to confuse Q with O. When he was fifteen, Louis invented an alphabet that used raised dots. It was a big success!

questions.stem: The Wright brothers failed many times before they flew an airplane.
Before Louis Braille’s invention it was difficult for blind children to read.
Louis Braille invented an alphabet with raised letters.

passage.title: Electric Skateboards
paragraphs: Electric skateboards are a great invention! The first electric skateboard, or eboard, was built by Louie Finkle in 1997. Finkle was an inventor who used to take apart machines so he could learn about them. This helped him understand how to build an eboard.

It was difficult to create a battery-powered skateboard back then. The batteries and motors weren’t strong enough. This made Finkle’s skateboard expensive. It cost $995. It took 15 years to solve this problem. Around 2005, new inventions made it possible to build an eboard with a stronger battery. Now there are a lot of inventors trying to create the fastest, cheapest, or lightest electric skateboard. Today you can buy an eboard for as little as $200.

An electric skateboard has a controller which you use to go slow or fast and to brake. Old-fashioned skateboards used to have four wheels. Some of the newer eboards only have one big wheel. These eboards can go up to 20 mph. So you’ll still need your helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads!

parts.name: Speaking with Dad
parts.sub: Dad asks, you answer out loud. 1 point each.
parts.imageAlt: A town with a park. A girl on a bicycle pulls a boy on a skateboard. A mother pushes a small child on a swing. A boy flies a kite. Children spin on a merry-go-round. Signs point to the mall, the zoo, the city center and the airport, and there is an ice cream shop and a toy store.
parts.caption: Look at the picture while Dad asks you.

prompts.q: Look at the girl on the bicycle. What is she doing with the boy on the skateboard?
prompts.a: She is pulling the boy on the skateboard.

prompts.q: If she rides the bike faster, what will happen to the boy?
prompts.a: The faster she rides, the faster the boy goes. / If she rides the bike faster, the boy will go faster.

prompts.q: What do you use to keep safe on a bike or skateboard?
prompts.a: You use a helmet / knee pads / elbow pads.

prompts.q: If you’re riding a bike and want to turn left, what do you do?
prompts.a: You turn your wheel to the left. / You lean to the left.

prompts.q: Are they riding toward the mall?
prompts.a: No, they’re riding away from the mall.

prompts.q: What is the mom in the park doing?
prompts.a: The mom is pushing the daughter (on the swings).
You push and pull your legs up and down.

prompts.q: The mom gave the boy the kite. What is another way to say that sentence using “to”?
prompts.a: The mom gave the kite to him / to the boy.

prompts.q: What are the children doing on the merry-go-round?
How can the children on the merry-go-round get dizzier?
prompts.a: The faster they go, the dizzier they get. / They can push more / faster.
